analyses.failure: CHK-001 (assertion) 'pcpi_wait stays asserted until pcpi_ready' — 2809 fails / 278073 hits, first fail at 480000 ps (sim.log:39). Fails also occur in groups exactly 370000 ps apart (sim.log:49-51: 19035000, 19405000, 19775000).
analyses.spec_says: spec/c_pcpi_div_Design_Specification.md:62-66 (rule PD-T1.1-06, SHOULD, rules.json:164-186): "A PCPI core that needs more than a couple of cycles to execute an instruction, should assert `pcpi_wait` as soon as the instruction has been decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts `pcpi_ready`." Master side (PD-T1.1-01, spec :48-52) only says pcpi_valid is asserted with the instruction. The spec never says whether the master must drop pcpi_valid between two instructions. contract.json:327 (assumption) says: "Legal master stimulus holds pcpi_valid ... stable from issue until pcpi_ready=1 is sampled, and deasserts pcpi_valid on the following cycle." contract.json:223 (CHK-008 stimulus) says: "then drive pcpi_valid=0 on the next cycle". The reference master in rtl/picorv32.v:1598-1603 and :1770-1775 does `pcpi_valid <= 0` when it sees pcpi_int_ready, then goes to cpu_state_fetch. So the real core always gives at least one edge with pcpi_valid=0 between PCPI instructions. rules.json:720-721 records the open question on PD-T1.1-06 timing ('more than a couple of cycles', 'as soon as').
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/picorv32.v:2444-2451 registers instr_div/divu/rem/remu every cycle where `pcpi_valid && !pcpi_ready` and the opcode matches. They clear the cycle after an edge with pcpi_ready=1. rtl/picorv32.v:2453 `pcpi_wait <= instr_any_div_rem && resetn;` makes pcpi_wait the decode flag delayed by one more register. rtl/picorv32.v:2480-2483 sets pcpi_ready/pcpi_wr for one cycle on completion. Call R_c the edge where pcpi_ready=1 is sampled. Then instr_any=1 at R_c (it was set at R_c-1, where ready was still 0), so pcpi_wait is still 1 at R_c+1: a trailing one-cycle pulse after ready. It is 0 at R_c+2. In the failing cycles the DUT sees pcpi_valid=1 at R_c+1 with a new instruction. At R_c+1 the antecedent is true (valid=1, wait=1 from the trailing pulse, ready=0). At R_c+2 wait=0 and ready=0, so the assertion fires. At R_c+3 pcpi_wait rises again and wait_q=0, so start fires (2436, 2472) and the new division runs and gives the right result: CHK-002/003 0 fails, all 7 tests pass (results.json:15-49). With at least one valid=0 edge between instructions, the trailing pulse falls on an edge with pcpi_valid=0 and the antecedent is false. Note that this RTL is upstream PicoRV32 code (spec header line 1 cites commit ef203c2).
analyses.test_does: verif/tests/test_c_pcpi_div.py:214-217: after the ready edge, execute() does `await next_cycle; self.drive(0); self.sample(chk)` and returns without waiting for another cycle. idle(gap) (160-167) does `next_cycle` then drive for each of gap iterations, so with gap=0 it does nothing. The next execute() then calls `self.drive(1, insn, rs1, rs2)` at line 181 in the same mid-cycle, which overwrites the pcpi_valid=0 just written. The DUT therefore never samples the deassert cycle. In general the DUT sees only `gap` edges of valid=0 instead of gap+1. gap=0 is common: CHK-004 randint(0,2) (273), CHK-005 randint(0,3) (295), CHK-008 gap in (0,1,5) (329), regression 50% gap=0 (395-396). The Python model still records self.valid=0 for that cycle (131), so its own CHK-003 check (154-157) and its wait check (186-206) do not see a problem. The wait sampled at the issue edge (182) is never checked, and first_wait is only tracked from j=1. Evidence that the deassert edge is missing: latency is 36 edges (sim.log:35). With a real valid=0 edge, back-to-back instructions repeat every 38 edges (380 ns at the 10 ns clock implied by 26 cases × ~38 edges ≈ 9975 ns). The log shows failures exactly 370000 ps (37 edges) apart (sim.log:49-51, 70-74, 104-107). In results.json:201,225, COVP-029 'Back-to-back division requests' (nnc_cov.sv:143-144: valid && is_div && !prev_out && prev_ready_q, so valid high right after a ready edge) = 2809. COVP-005 'Wait high in first cycle of a division request' = 2809. Both equal the CHK-001 fail count exactly. The first fail at 480 ns falls inside test_chk_004 (0–9975 ns); its sim.log line comes after the test-start banner only because of output ordering.

candidates.evidence_for: Contract stimulus (contract.json:223) and assumption (contract.json:327) need pcpi_valid=0 on the cycle after the ready edge. The test intends this (comment at test_c_pcpi_div.py:214 'Next cycle: deassert pcpi_valid'), but the drive(0) at :216 is overwritten by drive(1) at :181 in the same mid-cycle when gap=0. So the DUT sees pcpi_valid held high across two instructions. That is master behaviour the reference core never produces (picorv32.v:1600, 1772 deassert pcpi_valid and go to fetch). Fail count = COVP-029 back-to-back count = COVP-005 = 2809. Fail spacing is 37 edges (= 36-edge latency + 1), not 38, which shows there is no idle edge. The data path works in these cases (all result checks pass).
candidates.evidence_against: The nnc_cocotb next_cycle() helper is not in this directory, so the exact way writes in the same timestep are merged is inferred from the docstring (test:3-6) and the 37-edge spacing, not read directly. The spec itself does not forbid holding pcpi_valid across back-to-back instructions.

candidates.evidence_for: pcpi_wait is two registers behind the decode (picorv32.v:2444, 2453) and is not cleared by pcpi_ready, so it stays 1 for one edge after pcpi_ready. PD-T1.1-06 says keep wait asserted 'until it asserts pcpi_ready', not after. If a master issues a new instruction on that edge, the DUT shows wait=1 and then drops it to 0 for one edge before raising it again, which breaks the 'stay asserted' pattern for the new instruction.
candidates.evidence_against: For every instruction, pcpi_wait stays high from its first assertion until pcpi_ready (test CHK-008(b) passes, results.json:36-39). The drop only happens when the master holds pcpi_valid high across the ready edge, which contract.json:327 excludes as legal stimulus and the reference core never does (picorv32.v:1598-1603). All results, the CHK-002/003 assertions and the 16-cycle acknowledge bound pass. The code is unmodified upstream PicoRV32.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec (c_pcpi_div_Design_Specification.md:48-66) does not say whether pcpi_valid must drop between instructions, or what pcpi_wait may do after pcpi_ready. The 'no back-to-back valid' rule comes only from a contract assumption (contract.json:327) and the core RTL, not from spec text. rules.json:720-721 already marks the PD-T1.1-06 timing as not settled.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract does settle the stimulus constraint explicitly (contract.json:223, 327), and the test was meant to follow it. The failure comes from the test not doing what the contract says, not from the contract and spec disagreeing.

analyses.options: Fix test: make sure at least one rising edge samples pcpi_valid=0 between instructions, as contract.json:223/327 require. For example, at the end of execute() (test_c_pcpi_div.py:214-217), or at the start of execute() before drive(1) at :181, add an `await next_cycle(self.dut)` so the deassert drive is not overwritten in the same mid-cycle. Alternatively, have idle() always run at least one cycle. Also check the wait sampled at the issue edge, or keep the Python shadow self.valid consistent with what the DUT actually sees, so the test's own checks would catch this mismatch. Expected result: CHK-001 fails drop to 0, and back-to-back spacing becomes 38 edges. Fix RTL, only if the designer wants to support masters that hold pcpi_valid across consecutive instructions: clear pcpi_wait on completion so it does not lag pcpi_ready. For example, make picorv32.v:2453 `pcpi_wait <= instr_any_div_rem && resetn && !pcpi_ready;` or gate the decode/wait on completion, then re-check that the start pulse (2436) still fires for the next instruction. This changes upstream code. Clarify spec: add a stated master rule (e.g. 'pcpi_valid is deasserted for at least one cycle after pcpi_ready', which matches picorv32.v:1600/1772), or say explicitly that back-to-back valid is allowed and what pcpi_wait may do on the edge after pcpi_ready. Then align contract.json:327 and the test with it. The check itself should stay as it is.
